claim: CED-1 is a phagocytic receptor that mediates apoptotic cell recognition by phagocytic cells in Caenorhabditis elegans.
source: The phagocytic receptor CED-1 mediates apoptotic cell recognition by phagocytic cells, enabling cell corpse clearance in Caenorhabditis elegans.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a known function of CED-1.

claim: TRIM-21 is an E3 ubiquitin ligase that functions as a component of the CED-1 pathway for apoptotic cell clearance in C. elegans.
source: Here, we identified the C. elegans E3 ubiquitin ligase tripartite motif containing-21 (TRIM-21) as a component of the CED-1 pathway for apoptotic cell clearance.
evidence: This is a primary finding reported in the abstract based on experimental identification.

claim: TRIM-21 functions in conjunction with UBC-21 to catalyze K48-linked poly-ubiquitination on CED-1.
source: TRIM-21 functioned in conjunction with UBC-21 to catalyze K48-linked poly-ubiquitination on CED-1, targeting it for proteasomal degradation.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a finding from the study.

claim: K48-linked poly-ubiquitination of CED-1 by TRIM-21 and UBC-21 targets CED-1 for proteasomal degradation.
source: TRIM-21 functioned in conjunction with UBC-21 to catalyze K48-linked poly-ubiquitination on CED-1, targeting it for proteasomal degradation.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a finding from the study.

claim: The NPXY motif of CED-1 binds to the adaptor protein CED-6.
source: When the NPXY motif of CED-1 was bound to the adaptor protein CED-6 or the YXXL motif of CED-1 was phosphorylated by tyrosine kinase SRC-1 and subsequently bound to the adaptor protein NCK-1 containing the SH2 domain, TRIM-21 functioned in conjunction with UBC-21 to catalyze K48-linked poly-ubiquitination on CED-1
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a condition for TRIM-21 function.

claim: The YXXL motif of CED-1 is phosphorylated by tyrosine kinase SRC-1.
source: When the NPXY motif of CED-1 was bound to the adaptor protein CED-6 or the YXXL motif of CED-1 was phosphorylated by tyrosine kinase SRC-1 and subsequently bound to the adaptor protein NCK-1 containing the SH2 domain, TRIM-21 functioned in conjunction with UBC-21 to catalyze K48-linked poly-ubiquitination on CED-1
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a finding from the study.

claim: Phosphorylated YXXL motif of CED-1 binds to the adaptor protein NCK-1 containing the SH2 domain.
source: When the NPXY motif of CED-1 was bound to the adaptor protein CED-6 or the YXXL motif of CED-1 was phosphorylated by tyrosine kinase SRC-1 and subsequently bound to the adaptor protein NCK-1 containing the SH2 domain, TRIM-21 functioned in conjunction with UBC-21 to catalyze K48-linked poly-ubiquitination on CED-1
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a finding from the study.

claim: In the absence of TRIM-21, CED-1 accumulates post-translationally.
source: In the absence of TRIM-21, CED-1 accumulated post-translationally and drove cell corpse degradation defects, as evidenced by direct binding to VHA-10.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a finding from the study.

claim: Accumulated CED-1 in trim-21 mutants drives cell corpse degradation defects.
source: In the absence of TRIM-21, CED-1 accumulated post-translationally and drove cell corpse degradation defects, as evidenced by direct binding to VHA-10.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a finding from the study.

claim: Accumulated CED-1 in trim-21 mutants directly binds to VHA-10.
source: In the absence of TRIM-21, CED-1 accumulated post-translationally and drove cell corpse degradation defects, as evidenced by direct binding to VHA-10.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a finding from the study.

claim: When C. elegans cells undergo apoptosis, CED-8 activation by CED-3 produces phosphatidylserine (PS) on the cell surface.
source: When Caenorhabditis elegans cells undergo apoptosis, the activation of CED-8 by CED-3 produces phosphatidylserine (PS) on the cell surface, acting as an 'eat-me' signal that is recognized by phagocytes to activate two parallel, redundant genetic pathways (Huang et al., 2012; Suzuki et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Phosphatidylserine on the apoptotic cell surface acts as an 'eat-me' signal recognized by phagocytes.
source: When Caenorhabditis elegans cells undergo apoptosis, the activation of CED-8 by CED-3 produces phosphatidylserine (PS) on the cell surface, acting as an 'eat-me' signal that is recognized by phagocytes to activate two parallel, redundant genetic pathways (Huang et al., 2012; Suzuki et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: The ced-2/5/12 pathway mediates activation of the small GTPase CED-10/Rac1 for actin cytoskeleton rearrangement during cell corpse engulfment.
source: The ced-2/5/12 pathway mediates the activation of the small GTPase CED-10/Rac1, leading to rearrangement of the actin cytoskeleton for cell corpse engulfment (Wang et al., 2003).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: TTR-52 binds to both exposed PS and the extracellular domain of CED-1, acting as a bridging molecule.
source: In the ced-1/6/7 pathway, TTR-52 binds to both exposed PS and the extracellular domain of CED-1, acting as a bridging molecule to cross-link PS with CED-1 (Wang et al., 2010; Zhou et al., 2001).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: CED-7 is a homolog of the mammalian ABC transporter.
source: CED-7, a homolog of the mammalian ABC transporter, functions in both dying and engulfing cells, is required for the enrichment of CED-1 around cell corpses (Mapes et al., 2012; Wu and Horvitz, 1998).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: CED-7 functions in both dying and engulfing cells and is required for enrichment of CED-1 around cell corpses.
source: CED-7, a homolog of the mammalian ABC transporter, functions in both dying and engulfing cells, is required for the enrichment of CED-1 around cell corpses (Mapes et al., 2012; Wu and Horvitz, 1998).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: CED-6 interacts with the cytoplasmic tail of CED-1 through its phosphotyrosine-binding domain (PTB).
source: After the phagocytic receptor CED-1 recognizes PS, the adaptor protein CED-6 (GULP) interacts with the cytoplasmic tail of CED-1 through its phosphotyrosine-binding domain (PTB) to transduce engulfment signals to downstream effectors (Liu and Hengartner, 1998; Su et al., 2002)
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: CED-6 transduces engulfment signals to downstream effectors including DYN-1, clathrin, and clathrin adaptors AP2 or epsin.
source: After the phagocytic receptor CED-1 recognizes PS, the adaptor protein CED-6 (GULP) interacts with the cytoplasmic tail of CED-1 through its phosphotyrosine-binding domain (PTB) to transduce engulfment signals to downstream effectors (Liu and Hengartner, 1998; Su et al., 2002), including the large GTPase dynamin (DYN-1) (Yu et al., 2006), clathrin, and clarithin adaptors AP2 or epsin (Chen et al., 2013; Shen et al., 2013), to promote actin rearrangement for the internalization of ACs.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Phagosomes fuse with lysosomes to form phagolysosomes that digest corpses using lysosomal acid hydrolases.
source: The phagosomes then fuse with lysosomes to form phagolysosomes that digest corpses using lysosomal acid hydrolases (Kinchen et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: CED-1 shares sequence similarity with MEGF10 and Jedi in mammals and Draper in Drosophila.
source: CED-1 shares a sequence similarity with several cell surface proteins, including multiple EGF-like domains 10 (MEGF10) (Kay et al., 2012) and Jedi in mammals (Wu et al., 2009) and Draper in Drosophila (Ziegenfuss et al., 2008), all of which have been implicated in the recognition of ACs.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: MEGF10, Jedi, and Draper have been implicated in the recognition of apoptotic cells.
source: CED-1 shares a sequence similarity with several cell surface proteins, including multiple EGF-like domains 10 (MEGF10) (Kay et al., 2012) and Jedi in mammals (Wu et al., 2009) and Draper in Drosophila (Ziegenfuss et al., 2008), all of which have been implicated in the recognition of ACs.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: The CED-1 receptor is recycled from the phagosome back to the cell membrane by the retromer complex.
source: Our previous work showed that the CED-1 receptor is recycled from the phagosome back to the cell membrane by the retromer complex.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as previous work by the authors.

claim: Loss of function of the retromer results in lysosomal degradation of CED-1.
source: The recycling of CED-1 by the retromer complex is critical for AC clearance as the loss of function of the retromer results in the lysosomal degradation of CED-1 (Chen et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: In Drosophila glial cells, Draper intracellular domain promotes phagocytosis through an ITAM-domain-SFK-Syk-mediated signaling cascade.
source: In Drosophila glial cells, Draper intracellular domain promotes phagocytosis through an ITAM-domain-SFK-Syk-mediated signaling cascade (Ziegenfuss et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: The transcriptional factor STAT92e promotes clearance of degenerating axonal debris by directly activating transcriptional expression of Draper.
source: And the transcriptional factor STAT92e promotes the clearance of degenerating axonal debris by directly activating the transcriptional expression of Draper (Musashe et al., 2016; Purice et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: The transcriptional factor Serpent is required for sufficient phagocytosis of ACs in Drosophila embryonic macrophages through Draper regulation.
source: Recently, the transcriptional factor Serpent, a GATA factor homolog (Waltzer et al., 2016), was observed to be required for sufficient phagocytosis of ACs in Drosophila embryonic macrophages through the Draper regulation (Kurant et al., 2008; Shlyakhover et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Bfc serves as a Serpent co-factor to upregulate transcription of the engulfment receptor Croquemort in Drosophila macrophages.
source: Our recent study also showed that Bfc serves as a Serpent co-factor to upregulate transcription of the engulfment receptor Croquemort, and thus boosts macrophage efferocytosis in response to excessive apoptosis in Drosophila (Zheng et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: Pretreatment of wild-type C. elegans with chloroquine led to a marked increase in endogenous levels of CED-1.
source: We found that pretreatment of wild-type (WT) C. elegans with CQ led to a marked increase in the endogenous levels of CED-1 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a finding from the study shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: CED-1 undergoes lysosome-mediated degradation.
source: These results suggest that although CED-1 is recycled to the cell membrane during phagocytosis of the cell corpse (Chen et al., 2010), the remaining CED-1 still undergoes lysosome-mediated degradation.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the chloroquine treatment results with reference to previous work.

claim: Endogenous CED-1 accumulated to higher levels with increasing doses of MG132 in WT worms.
source: In WT worms pre-treated with different concentrations of the proteasome inhibitor MG132, we observed that endogenous CED-1 accumulated to higher levels with increasing doses of MG132 (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is a finding from the study shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Endogenous levels of CED-1 were significantly increased in uba-1 and ubq-2 RNAi knockdown lines compared to WT controls.
source: We then generated C. elegans RNAi knocked down for either the sole E1 enzyme gene uba-1 or the single-copy ubiquitin gene ubq-2 and found that endogenous levels of CED-1 were significantly increased compared to WT controls in both of these transient suppression lines (Figure 1B)
evidence: This is a finding from the study shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The proteasomal pathway is involved in CED-1 degradation.
source: We then generated C. elegans RNAi knocked down for either the sole E1 enzyme gene uba-1 or the single-copy ubiquitin gene ubq-2 and found that endogenous levels of CED-1 were significantly increased compared to WT controls in both of these transient suppression lines (Figure 1B), suggesting that the proteasomal pathway was involved in CED-1 degradation.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the RNAi knockdown results.

claim: Endogenous levels of CED-1 were significantly increased after treatment with CQ and MG132 overlay compared to CQ or MG132 treatment alone.
source: To examine the relationship between lysosome- and proteasome-dependent CED-1 degradation, we treated C. elegans with CQ and MG132 overlay and found that endogenous levels of CED-1 were significantly increased compared to those after CQ or MG132 treatment (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a finding from the study shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: CED-1 is poly-ubiquitinated in C. elegans.
source: Anti-FLAG immunoprecipitates with antibodies against ubiquitin (Ub) revealed several poly-ubiquitinated forms of CED-1 (Figure 1C), confirming that CED-1 was indeed poly-ubiquitinated in the worms.
evidence: This is a finding from the study shown in Figure 1C.

claim: CED-1 acts as a substrate for poly-ubiquitylation and is degraded by the ubiquitin-proteasome pathway.
source: These observations confirmed that CED-1 acted as a substrate for poly-ubiquitylation and was degraded by the ubiquitin-proteasome pathway.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the ubiquitination and proteasome inhibition experiments.

claim: Inactivation of b0281.8, k01g5.1, and f43c11.7 resulted in accumulation of significantly higher endogenous CED-1 protein levels in all three replicates.
source: We found that the inactivation of three potential E3 ligases, b0281.8, k01g5.1, and f43c11.7, resulted in the accumulation of significantly higher endogenous CED-1 protein levels in all three replicates (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is a finding from the RNAi screen shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Only b0281.8 interacted with CED-1 in yeast two-hybrid assays among the three E3 ligase candidates.
source: Among these three candidates, only b0281.8 interacted with CED-1 in yeast two-hybrid (Y2H) assays (Figure 1E, Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is a finding from the Y2H assays shown in Figure 1E and Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: B0281.8 is an ortholog of human TRIM21 containing an N-terminal RING finger domain, a BBox domain, and a C-terminal α-helical coiled-coil domain.
source: The analysis of the B0281.8 sequence showed that this E3 UB-ligase was an ortholog of human TRIM21 containing an N-terminal RING finger domain, a BBox domain, and a C-terminal α-helical coiled-coil domain (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A and B)
evidence: This is a finding from sequence analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A and B.

claim: Recombinant CED-1 protein was pulled down by GST-TRIM-21 but not by GST.
source: Recombinant CED-1 protein was pulled down by GST-TRIM-21 but not by GST, indicating that TRIM-21 could directly interact with CED-1 (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is a finding from GST pull-down assays shown in Figure 1F.

claim: TRIM-21 directly interacts with CED-1 in vitro.
source: Recombinant CED-1 protein was pulled down by GST-TRIM-21 but not by GST, indicating that TRIM-21 could directly interact with CED-1 (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the GST pull-down results.

claim: CED-1 was immunoprecipitated from heat shock-treated worm lysates using FLAG antibodies but not from untreated control lysates.
source: To further determine whether TRIM-21 also interacts with CED-1 in vivo, we generated an integrated transgenic strain xwhIs28(Phsp-16trim-21::flag) that expressed a TRIM-21-FLAG fusion protein under the control of a heat shock promoter and found that CED-1 was immunoprecipitated from heat shock-treated worm lysates using FLAG antibodies, but not from untreated control lysates (Figure 1G).
evidence: This is a finding from co-IP experiments shown in Figure 1G.

claim: TRIM-21 interacts with CED-1 in vivo.
source: These results confirmed that TRIM-21 interacts with CED-1 in vivo.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the co-IP experiments.

claim: The amino acid region between residues 931–1007 in the intracellular domain of CED-1 is sufficient to bind TRIM-21.
source: The results showed that the amino acid region between residues 931–1007 in the intracellular, but not extracellular, domain of CED-1 was sufficient to bind TRIM-21 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1F)
evidence: This is a finding from Y2H and GST pull-down assays shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1F.

claim: The coiled-coil domain of TRIM-21 is required for its interaction with CED-1.
source: and the coiled-coil domain of TRIM-21 was required for its interaction with CED-1 (Figure 1H, Figure 1—figure supplement 1G–I).
evidence: This is a finding from Y2H and GST pull-down assays shown in Figure 1H and Figure 1—figure supplement 1G–I.

claim: TRIM-21 interacted with full-length CED-1 but not with CED-1 variant harboring a C-terminal deletion.
source: Co-immunoprecipitation (co-IP) assays using an integrated C. elegans strain smIs34 expressing a full-length CED-1::GFP fusion protein under the native CED-1 promoter and a second integrated transgenic line, smIs110, which expressed a GFP-fused CED-1 with the C-terminal region deleted (CED-1ΔC::GFP), also driven by the native promoter, revealed that TRIM-21 interacted with the full-length CED-1, but not with the CED-1 variant harboring a C-terminal deletion (Figure 1I).
evidence: This is a finding from co-IP assays shown in Figure 1I.

claim: CED-1-TRIM-21 binding is mediated by the interaction between the CED-1 intracellular domain and the TRIM-21 coiled-coil domain.
source: These data demonstrated that CED-1-TRIM-21 binding was mediated by the interaction between the CED-1 intracellular domain and the TRIM-21 coiled-coil domain.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the truncation and co-IP experiments.

claim: hTRIM21 interacts with MEGF10-CT and CED-1-CT.
source: Interestingly, we found that hTRIM21 interacted with MEGF10-CT and CED-1-CT, whereas TRIM-21 interacted with CED-1-CT and MEGF10-CT, suggesting that TRIM-21 is an ancient E3 ligase in which the coiled-coil domain recognizes its substrate CED-1 (Figure 1—figure supplement 2D and E).
evidence: This is a finding from interaction assays shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2D and E.

claim: TRIM-21 is an ancient E3 ligase in which the coiled-coil domain recognizes its substrate CED-1.
source: Interestingly, we found that hTRIM21 interacted with MEGF10-CT and CED-1-CT, whereas TRIM-21 interacted with CED-1-CT and MEGF10-CT, suggesting that TRIM-21 is an ancient E3 ligase in which the coiled-coil domain recognizes its substrate CED-1 (Figure 1—figure supplement 2D and E).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the cross-species interaction results.

claim: CED-1 protein accumulated to significantly higher levels in worms carrying the trim-21(xwh12) allele than in those carrying the WT allele.
source: WB analysis indicated that CED-1 protein accumulated to significantly higher levels in worms carrying the trim-21(xwh12) allele than in those carrying the WT allele (Figure 1J)
evidence: This is a finding from Western blot analysis shown in Figure 1J.

claim: The transcription level of CED-1 was unaltered in trim-21(xwh12) mutants.
source: but the transcription level of CED-1 was unaltered (Figure 1K)
evidence: This is a finding from qRT-PCR shown in Figure 1K.

claim: TRIM-21 is required for CED-1 degradation.
source: WB analysis indicated that CED-1 protein accumulated to significantly higher levels in worms carrying the trim-21(xwh12) allele than in those carrying the WT allele (Figure 1J), but the transcription level of CED-1 was unaltered (Figure 1K), which further suggested that TRIM-21 was required for CED-1 degradation.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the Western blot and qRT-PCR results.

claim: Full-length CED-1::GFP in smIs34 and bcIs39 were higher in progeny carrying trim-21(xwh12) than in controls.
source: We observed that full-length CED-1::GFP in smIs34 and bcIs39, but not CED-1ΔC::GFP in smIs110, were higher in the progeny carrying trim-21(xwh12) than in the controls (Figure 1L)
evidence: This is a finding from Western blot analysis shown in Figure 1L.

claim: The CED-1 intracellular domain is required for its binding and degradation by TRIM-21.
source: We observed that full-length CED-1::GFP in smIs34 and bcIs39, but not CED-1ΔC::GFP in smIs110, were higher in the progeny carrying trim-21(xwh12) than in the controls (Figure 1L), which demonstrated that the CED-1 intracellular domain was required for its binding and degradation by TRIM-21.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the Western blot results with different CED-1 constructs.

claim: Endogenous levels of CED-1 were significantly higher after vps-37 knockdown in WT worms and trim-21 mutants than in controls.
source: Following knockdown of VPS-37, which blocks lysosomal degradation of CED-1 (Chen et al., 2010), in WT worms and the trim-21 mutant, the endogenous levels of CED-1 were significantly higher than those in the control (Figure 1M and N).
evidence: This is a finding from Western blot analysis shown in Figure 1M and N.

claim: TRIM-21 is an E3 ubiquitin ligase that interacts with CED-1 to mediate its degradation independently of lysosome-dependent degradation of CED-1.
source: Thus, TRIM-21 is an E3 ubiquitin ligase that interacted with CED-1 to mediate its degradation independently of lysosome-dependent degradation of CED-1.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the vps-37 knockdown experiments.

claim: Only inactivation of ubc-21 led to increased levels of endogenous CED-1 among 22 E2 ubiquitin-conjugating enzymes tested.
source: We found that only the inactivation of one candidate E2 enzyme, ubc-21, led to the increased levels of endogenous CED-1 (Table 2)
evidence: This is a finding from the E2 enzyme RNAi screen shown in Table 2.

claim: UBC-21 interacts with TRIM-21 in yeast two-hybrid assays.
source: and that UBC-21 apparently interacted with TRIM-21 in Y2H assays (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a finding from Y2H assays shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Recombinant TRIM-21 protein was pulled down by GST-UBC-21 but not by GST alone.
source: GST pull-down assays showed that the recombinant TRIM-21 protein could be pulled down by GST-UBC-21, but not by GST alone (Figure 2B)
evidence: This is a finding from GST pull-down assays shown in Figure 2B.

claim: TRIM-21 directly interacts with UBC-21 in vitro.
source: GST pull-down assays showed that the recombinant TRIM-21 protein could be pulled down by GST-UBC-21, but not by GST alone (Figure 2B), indicating that TRIM-21 directly interacted with UBC-21 in vitro.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the GST pull-down results.

claim: The coiled-coil domain of TRIM-21 interacts with UBC-21.
source: Using TRIM-21 truncation constructs in Y2H assays, we further observed that the coiled-coil domain of TRIM-21 interacted with UBC-21 (Figure 2C and D).
evidence: This is a finding from Y2H assays shown in Figure 2C and D.

claim: CED-1-CT was poly-ubiquitinated by purified HA-UBQ-2, UBA-1, UBC-21, and TRIM-21 in vitro.
source: To further investigate whether UBC-21 (E2) and TRIM-21 (E3) catalyzed poly-ubiquitin modification of CED-1, we performed in vitro ubiquitination assays using a CED-1 variant consisting of only the C-terminal intracellular domain (CED-1-CT) and found that it was poly-ubiquitinated by purified HA-UBQ-2, UBA-1, UBC-21, and TRIM-21.
evidence: This is a finding from in vitro ubiquitination assays.

claim: Poly-ubiquitination of CED-1-CT was completely abolished by removal of either UBC-21 or TRIM-21.
source: Notably, poly-ubiquitination of CED-1-CT was completely abolished by the removal of either UBC-21 or TRIM-21 (Figure 2E)
evidence: This is a finding from in vitro ubiquitination assays shown in Figure 2E.

claim: UBC-21 and TRIM-21 mediate poly-ubiquitination of CED-1-CT in vitro.
source: Notably, poly-ubiquitination of CED-1-CT was completely abolished by the removal of either UBC-21 or TRIM-21 (Figure 2E), indicating that UBC-21 and TRIM-21 mediated the poly-ubiquitination of CED-1-CT in vitro.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the in vitro ubiquitination results.

claim: CED-1 is poly-ubiquitinated in C. elegans in vivo.
source: Antibody detection of HA in immunoprecipitation lysates obtained from the recombinant progeny revealed a smear of high-molecular mass species (Figure 2F), indicating that CED-1 was poly-ubiquitinated in the worms.
evidence: This is a finding from co-IP experiments shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Poly-ubiquitination of CED-1 was greatly reduced in both ubc-21(lf) and trim-21(lf) mutants.
source: We then introduced ced-1::flag and ha::ubq-2 into the ubc-21(xwh15) (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C) and trim-21(xwh12) knockout strains and found that poly-ubiquitination of CED-1 was greatly reduced in both the ubc-21(lf) and trim-21(lf) mutants (Figure 2F and H).
evidence: This is a finding from co-IP experiments shown in Figure 2F and H.

claim: K48R- but not K63R-ubiquitin abolished poly-ubiquitination of CED-1-CT in vitro.
source: We found that inclusion of K48R- (conserved function in regulating protein degradation) but not K63R- (signal transduction) ubiquitin abolished poly-ubiquitination of CED-1-CT in vitro (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is a finding from in vitro ubiquitination assays shown in Figure 2E.

claim: K48R- but not K63R-ubiquitin abolished CED-1 poly-ubiquitination in vivo.
source: WB assays to detect ubiquitination of CED-1 by anti-FLAG immunoprecipitation showed that K48R-, but not K63R-, ubiquitin abolished CED-1 poly-ubiquitination in vivo (Figure 2G and H)
evidence: This is a finding from co-IP experiments shown in Figure 2G and H.

claim: CED-1 is modified by K48-linked but not K63-linked poly-ubiquitination.
source: WB assays to detect ubiquitination of CED-1 by anti-FLAG immunoprecipitation showed that K48R-, but not K63R-, ubiquitin abolished CED-1 poly-ubiquitination in vivo (Figure 2G and H), indicating that CED-1 was modified by K48-linked, but not K63-linked poly-ubiquitination.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the ubiquitination assays with different ubiquitin mutants.

claim: Ubiquitination of CED-1 by vps-37 knockdown was similar to that in the control.
source: Ubiquitination of CED-1 by vps-37 knockdown was similar to that in the control (Figure 2I and J)
evidence: This is a finding from co-IP experiments shown in Figure 2I and J.

claim: Lysosomal degradation of CED-1 does not affect poly-ubiquitination of CED-1.
source: Ubiquitination of CED-1 by vps-37 knockdown was similar to that in the control (Figure 2I and J), suggesting that lysosomal degradation of CED-1 does not affect poly-ubiquitination of CED-1.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the vps-37 knockdown ubiquitination results.

claim: UBC-21 and TRIM-21 together catalyze K48-linked poly-ubiquitination of CED-1.
source: Collectively, these observations demonstrated that UBC-21 and TRIM-21 together catalyzed K48-linked poly-ubiquitination of CED-1.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the ubiquitination experiments.

claim: CED-1 accumulated at higher levels in ced-3(n717), ced-4(n1162), ced-8(n1891), ced-7(n1892), and ced-6(n1813) mutants, as well as in ttr-52 RNAi-treated worms.
source: The results showed that CED-1 accumulated at higher levels in the ced-3(n717), ced-4(n1162), ced-8(n1891), ced-7(n1892), and ced-6(n1813) mutants, as well as in the ttr-52 RNAi-treated worms (Figure 3A, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A)
evidence: This is a finding from Western blot analysis shown in Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The core cell death machinery, surface-exposed PS on ACs, and CED-7/CED-6 pathways are required for CED-1 degradation.
source: The results showed that CED-1 accumulated at higher levels in the ced-3(n717), ced-4(n1162), ced-8(n1891), ced-7(n1892), and ced-6(n1813) mutants, as well as in the ttr-52 RNAi-treated worms (Figure 3A, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A), indicating that the core cell death machinery, surface-exposed PS on ACs, and CED-7/CED-6 pathways were required for CED-1 degradation, whereas the ced-2/5/12 pathway was not.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the Western blot results with different mutants.

claim: The ced-2/5/12 pathway is not required for CED-1 degradation.
source: The results showed that CED-1 accumulated at higher levels in the ced-3(n717), ced-4(n1162), ced-8(n1891), ced-7(n1892), and ced-6(n1813) mutants, as well as in the ttr-52 RNAi-treated worms (Figure 3A, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A), indicating that the core cell death machinery, surface-exposed PS on ACs, and CED-7/CED-6 pathways were required for CED-1 degradation, whereas the ced-2/5/12 pathway was not.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the Western blot results showing no effect of ced-2/5 mutations.

claim: No significant differences in CED-1 levels were observed between control RNAi-treated and dyn-1 or ap-2 RNAi-treated worms.
source: No significant differences in CED-1 levels were observed between control RNAi-treated and dyn-1 or ap-2 RNAi-treated worms (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B)
evidence: This is a finding from Western blot analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: CED-6 may perform the last step necessary for CED-1 degradation.
source: No significant differences in CED-1 levels were observed between control RNAi-treated and dyn-1 or ap-2 RNAi-treated worms (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B), suggesting that CED-6 may perform the last step necessary for CED-1 degradation.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the RNAi results showing no effect of downstream factors.

claim: Endogenous levels of CED-1 were significantly increased in both ced-6(lf) mutants when crossed with TRIM-21 overexpression strains.
source: By crossing the integrated transgenic strain xwhIs29(Pced-1trim-21::flag) expressing TRIM-21 under the control of the CED-1 promoter, and xwhIs28(Phsp-16trim-21::flag) expressing TRIM-21 under the control of the heat shock promoter with the ced-6(n1813) or ced-6(xwh25) mutant worms (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C), we found that the endogenous levels of CED-1 were significantly increased in both ced-6 (lf) mutants (Figure 3B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is a finding from Western blot analysis shown in Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1D.

claim: CED-6 function is required for TRIM-21-mediated CED-1 degradation in engulfing cells.
source: These findings indicated that the CED-6 function was required for TRIM-21-mediated CED-1 degradation in engulfing cells.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the genetic interaction results.

claim: Recombinant CED-6 protein was effectively co-immunoprecipitated with GST-TRIM-21 but not with GST alone.
source: Using GST pull-down assays, we found that recombinant CED-6 protein was effectively co-immunoprecipitated with GST-TRIM-21, but not with GST alone (Figure 3C)
evidence: This is a finding from GST pull-down assays shown in Figure 3C.

claim: CED-6 directly interacts with TRIM-21 in vitro.
source: Using GST pull-down assays, we found that recombinant CED-6 protein was effectively co-immunoprecipitated with GST-TRIM-21, but not with GST alone (Figure 3C), indicating that CED-6 directly interacted with TRIM-21 in vitro.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the GST pull-down results.

claim: TRIM-21 was immunoprecipitated from lysates of heat shock-treated worms using antibodies targeting CED-6 but not from lysates of untreated controls.
source: We then used the xwhIs28(Phsp-16tirm-21::flag) strain to further address whether CED-6 could interact with TRIM-21 in vivo. The results showed that TRIM-21 could be immunoprecipitated from lysates of heat shock-treated worms using antibodies targeting CED-6, but not from lysates of untreated controls (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is a finding from co-IP experiments shown in Figure 3D.

claim: CED-6 directly interacts with TRIM-21 in vivo.
source: Therefore, we determined that CED-6 directly interacted with TRIM-21 in vivo.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the co-IP experiments.

claim: The PTB domain of CED-6 is sufficient to bind TRIM-21.
source: To identify the region(s) of TRIM-21 and CED-6 participating in their binding interactions, we used Y2H and GST pull-down assays to examine CED-6 interactions with various TRIM-21 truncation variants. These experiments showed that the PTB domain of CED-6 was sufficient to bind TRIM-21, whereas the coiled-coil domain of TRIM-21 was required for its interaction with CED-6 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E and F).
evidence: This is a finding from Y2H and GST pull-down assays shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1E and F.

claim: The coiled-coil domain of TRIM-21 is required for its interaction with CED-6.
source: To identify the region(s) of TRIM-21 and CED-6 participating in their binding interactions, we used Y2H and GST pull-down assays to examine CED-6 interactions with various TRIM-21 truncation variants. These experiments showed that the PTB domain of CED-6 was sufficient to bind TRIM-21, whereas the coiled-coil domain of TRIM-21 was required for its interaction with CED-6 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E and F).
evidence: This is a finding from Y2H and GST pull-down assays shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1E and F.

claim: TRIM-21 does not function as an E3 ligase in CED-6 degradation.
source: Notably, we detected no increase in the endogenous protein levels of CED-6 in trim-21 (xwh12), indicating that TRIM-21 did not function as an E3 ligase in CED-6 degradation (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is a finding from Western blot analysis shown in Figure 3E.

claim: TRIM-21::mCherry or TRIM-21::GFP fusion reporter co-localized to the surface of cell corpses with CED-1::GFP and mCherry::CED-6 reporters in C. elegans.
source: Furthermore, fluorescence microscopy revealed that a TRIM-21::mCherry or TRIM-21::GFP fusion reporter co-localized to the surface of cell corpses with CED-1::GFP and mCherry::CED-6 reporters in C. elegans (Figure 3F).
evidence: This is a finding from fluorescence microscopy shown in Figure 3F.

claim: Recruitment of TRIM-21::GFP was significantly reduced in ced-6 mutants compared to in the WT.
source: We next examined whether CED-6 mediates TRIM-21 recruitment to the AC surface by detecting and quantifying TRIM-21::GFP recruitment to ACs in ced-6 mutants. We found that recruitment of TRIM-21::GFP was significantly reduced in ced-6 mutants compared to in the WT (Figure 3—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: This is a finding from fluorescence microscopy quantification shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1G.

claim: Co-localization of CED-1::GFP and TRIM-21::mCherry was greatly decreased in ced-6 mutants compared to that in the WT.
source: In addition, co-localization of CED-1::GFP and TRIM-21::mCherry was greatly decreased in ced-6 mutants compared to that in the WT (Figure 3F and G).
evidence: This is a finding from fluorescence microscopy shown in Figure 3F and G.

claim: CED-6 mediates recruitment of TRIM-21 to the AC surface.
source: These results indicate that CED-6 mediated recruitment of TRIM-21 to the AC surface.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the co-localization and recruitment results.

claim: The CED-6 PTB domain is sufficient to interact with the intracellular domain of CED-1 (CED-1-CT).
source: Y2H assays showed that the CED-6 PTB domain was sufficient to interact with the intracellular domain of CED-1(CED-1-CT) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1I).
evidence: This is a finding from Y2H assays shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1I.

claim: Recombinant CED-6 was successfully pulled down by GST-CED-1-CT but not by GST.
source: Moreover, recombinant CED-6 was successfully pulled down by GST-CED-1-CT, but not by GST (Figure 3—figure supplement 1H).
evidence: This is a finding from GST pull-down assays shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1H.

claim: N962A and Y965F mutations in CED-1 did not attenuate the engulfment defects of ced-1(e1735) mutants.
source: We then determined the number of ACs in developmental stages in embryos and found that N962A and Y965F did not attenuate the engulfment defects of ced-1(e1735) mutants (Table 3)
evidence: This is a finding from cell corpse counting shown in Table 3.

claim: N962 and Y965 residues are necessary for complete engulfment of CED-1.
source: We then determined the number of ACs in developmental stages in embryos and found that N962A and Y965F did not attenuate the engulfment defects of ced-1(e1735) mutants (Table 3), indicating that both residues were necessary for complete engulfment of CED-1, which was consistent with the results of a previous study (Zhou et al., 2001).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the cell corpse counting results with reference to previous work.

claim: The N962A CED-1 mutant exhibited severely impaired binding to CED-6.
source: GST pull-down and Y2H assays showed that the N962A CED-1 mutants exhibited severely impaired binding to CED-6, whereas the Y965F and Y1019F mutants of CED-1 bound successfully (Figure 3H, Figure 3—figure supplement 1I)
evidence: This is a finding from GST pull-down and Y2H assays shown in Figure 3H and Figure 3—figure supplement 1I.

claim: Y965F and Y1019F mutants of CED-1 bound successfully to CED-6.
source: GST pull-down and Y2H assays showed that the N962A CED-1 mutants exhibited severely impaired binding to CED-6, whereas the Y965F and Y1019F mutants of CED-1 bound successfully (Figure 3H, Figure 3—figure supplement 1I)
evidence: This is a finding from GST pull-down and Y2H assays shown in Figure 3H and Figure 3—figure supplement 1I.

claim: The interaction between CED-1 and CED-6 occurs through CED-6 binding to the CED-1 NPXY motif, and tyrosine phosphorylation is not a requirement for NPXY binding to CED-6.
source: GST pull-down and Y2H assays showed that the N962A CED-1 mutants exhibited severely impaired binding to CED-6, whereas the Y965F and Y1019F mutants of CED-1 bound successfully (Figure 3H, Figure 3—figure supplement 1I), suggesting that although the interaction occurred through CED-6 binding to the CED-1 NPXY motif, tyrosine phosphorylation was not a requirement for NPXY binding to CED-6.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the binding assays with different CED-1 mutants.

claim: CED-1 levels were higher in the N962A mutants than in the WT CED-1 controls.
source: Next, we addressed whether N962A mutations in the NPXY domain of CED-1 affected its protein levels. We found that the CED-1 levels were higher in the N962A mutants than in the WT CED-1 controls (Figure 3I).
evidence: This is a finding from Western blot analysis shown in Figure 3I.

claim: The binding of TRIM-21 to CED-1 was substantially reduced in the ced-6(xwh25) background.
source: In addition, we found that the binding of TRIM-21 to CED-1 was substantially reduced in the ced-6(xwh25) background (Figure 3J and K).
evidence: This is a finding from co-IP experiments shown in Figure 3J and K.

claim: Poly-ubiquitination of CED-1 was reduced in ced-6(xwh25) mutants.
source: Moreover, we found that the poly-ubiquitination of CED-1 was also reduced in ced-6(xwh25) mutants (Figure 3K and L).
evidence: This is a finding from co-IP experiments shown in Figure 3K and L.

claim: CED-6 mediates TRIM-21 binding interactions with CED-1 to ensure CED-1 degradation in vivo.
source: These results indicated that CED-6 mediated TRIM-21 binding interactions with CED-1 to ensure CED-1 degradation in vivo.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the binding and ubiquitination results in ced-6 mutants.

claim: SRC-1 is the only CED-1-CT-interacting tyrosine kinase identified by Y2H assay among 13 candidate tyrosine kinases.
source: To screen tyrosine kinases in C. elegans, we generated individual RNAi knockdowns of 90 potential tyrosine kinases and screened for germline cell death in three replicate experiments. We found that the inactivation of 13 candidate tyrosine kinases increased the cell corpse number in the germline (Table 4). Among these, SRC-1 was the only CED-1-CT-interacting tyrosine kinase identified by the Y2H assay (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is a finding from the tyrosine kinase RNAi screen and Y2H assays shown in Table 4 and Figure 4A.

claim: Recombinant SRC-1 protein was pulled down by GST-CED-1-CT but not by GST alone.
source: Furthermore, we found that the recombinant SRC-1 protein could be pulled down by GST-CED-1-CT, but not by GST alone (Figure 4B)
evidence: This is a finding from GST pull-down assays shown in Figure 4B.

claim: SRC-1 directly interacts with the CED-1 C-terminal intracellular domain.
source: Furthermore, we found that the recombinant SRC-1 protein could be pulled down by GST-CED-1-CT, but not by GST alone (Figure 4B), indicating that SRC-1 directly interacted with the CED-1 C-terminal intracellular domain.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the GST pull-down results.

claim: The CED-1 C-terminal domain interacts with SRC-1 as confirmed by TurboID proximity labeling.
source: Tagging CED-1-CT with TurboID ligase, an enzyme-catalyzed proximity biotin label for detecting direct protein interaction, further confirmed that the CED-1 C-terminal domain could interact with SRC-1 (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is a finding from TurboID proximity labeling shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Both the SH2 and SH3 domains of SRC-1 are required for interaction with the CED-1 intracellular domain.
source: Subsequent Y2H assays indicated that both the SH2 and SH3 domains of SRC-1 were required for interaction with the CED-1 intracellular domain (Figure 4D, Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a finding from Y2H assays shown in Figure 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Endogenous levels of CED-1 were higher in src-1(xwh26) knockout worms than in controls.
source: We used CRISPR-Cas9 to generate a mutant allele of src-1(xwh26), in which a premature stop codon was introduced at the N-terminus in WT worms (Figure 4—figure supplement 1F). We found that endogenous levels of CED-1 were higher in the src-1(xwh26) knockout worms than those in the control (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is a finding from Western blot analysis shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Poly-ubiquitination of CED-1 was attenuated in src-1-silenced worms.
source: Moreover, we found that poly-ubiquitination of CED-1 was attenuated in src-1-silenced worms (Figure 4F).
evidence: This is a finding from co-IP experiments shown in Figure 4F.

claim: SRC-1 is required for CED-1 degradation via the proteasome pathway.
source: These results confirmed that SRC-1 was required for CED-1 degradation via the proteasome pathway.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the src-1 mutant results.

claim: src-1 knockdown led to increased cell corpse numbers in both ced-2(n1994) and ced-1(e1735) mutants.
source: Moreover, we observed that src-1 knockdown led to increased cell corpse numbers in both ced-2(n1994) and ced-1(e1735) mutants (Figure 4G and H)
evidence: This is a finding from cell corpse counting shown in Figure 4G and H.

claim: src-1 does not act specifically within either engulfment pathway to regulate cell corpse removal.
source: Moreover, we observed that src-1 knockdown led to increased cell corpse numbers in both ced-2(n1994) and ced-1(e1735) mutants (Figure 4G and H), suggesting that src-1 did not act specifically within either pathway to regulate cell corpse removal.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the genetic interaction results.

claim: Tyr-1019 in CED-1-CT has substantially greater phosphorylation than other sites as identified by LC-MS/MS.
source: To identify the specific sites in the CED-1 intracellular domain (CED-1-CT) phosphorylated by SRC-1, we performed in vitro kinase assays, excising the CED-1-CT bands from the SDS-PAGE gel and purifying them for analysis by liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS). This assay revealed that one amino acid had substantially greater phosphorylation than the other sites: Tyr-1019 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: This is a finding from LC-MS/MS analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1G.

claim: Tyr-1019 is the predicted tyrosine phosphorylation site in the YXXL motif of the CED-1 intracellular domain.
source: Notably, this residue was the same as the predicted tyrosine phosphorylation site in the YXXL motif (residues 1019–1022) of the CED-1 intracellular domain (Zhou et al., 2001).
evidence: This is stated with reference to previous work.

claim: The Y1019F variant of CED-1 did not rescue the engulfment defects observed in ced-1(e1735) mutants.
source: To test the effects of abolishing this site, we generated a non-synonymous mutation that converted the conserved YXXL tyrosine residue (Y1019) to phenylalanine and found that the Y1019F variant did not rescue the engulfment defects observed in ced-1(e1735) mutants (Table 3).
evidence: This is a finding from cell corpse counting shown in Table 3.

claim: Y1019 residue is necessary for the engulfment activity mediated by CED-1.
source: These results indicated that this residue was necessary for the engulfment activity mediated by CED-1, which is consistent with the findings of a previous study (Zhou et al., 2001).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the Y1019F mutant results with reference to previous work.

claim: Less Pro-Q Diamond staining and decreased phosphorylation of CED-1 was observed when CED-1(Y1019F) variant was incubated with SRC-1.
source: We then asked whether the Y1019F mutation affected CED-1 phosphorylation by SRC-1. We found less Pro-Q Diamond staining and decreased phosphorylation of CED-1, assessed by anti-PY antibody, when the CED-1(Y1019F) variant was incubated with SRC-1, thus confirming that SRC-1 phosphorylated CED-1 at the Y1019 tyrosine residue (Figure 4I).
evidence: This is a finding from in vitro kinase assays shown in Figure 4I.

claim: SRC-1 phosphorylates CED-1 at the Y1019 tyrosine residue.
source: We found less Pro-Q Diamond staining and decreased phosphorylation of CED-1, assessed by anti-PY antibody, when the CED-1(Y1019F) variant was incubated with SRC-1, thus confirming that SRC-1 phosphorylated CED-1 at the Y1019 tyrosine residue (Figure 4I).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the in vitro kinase assays.

claim: The CED-1(Y1019F) variant can still bind to CED-6 or TRIM-21.
source: Y2H and GST pull-down assays showed that the CED-1(Y1019F) variant could still bind to CED-6 or TRIM-21 (Figure 3H, Figure 4—figure supplement 1H and I)
evidence: This is a finding from Y2H and GST pull-down assays shown in Figure 3H and Figure 4—figure supplement 1H and I.

claim: Tyrosine phosphorylation is not required for YXXL-mediated binding to CED-6 or TRIM-21.
source: Y2H and GST pull-down assays showed that the CED-1(Y1019F) variant could still bind to CED-6 or TRIM-21 (Figure 3H, Figure 4—figure supplement 1H and I), which suggested that tyrosine phosphorylation was not required for YXXL-mediated binding to CED-6 or TRIM-21.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the binding assays with Y1019F mutant.

claim: The degradation rates of the N962A and Y1019F CED-1 mutants were lower than those of WT CED-1.
source: Next, to address whether mutations in the N962 and Y1019 residues affected CED-1 protein stability, we introduced N962A(xwh21) and Y1019F(xwh22) mutations individually into the C. elegans genome at the ced-1 locus in the ced-1::flag(xwh18) strain (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C). We found that the degradation rates of the N962A and Y1019F CED-1 mutants were lower than those of WT CED-1 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1J and K).
evidence: This is a finding from CHX chase experiments shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1J and K.

claim: Poly-ubiquitination of CED-1 was reduced in the N962A and Y1019F mutants.
source: Moreover, we found that poly-ubiquitination of CED-1 was also reduced in the N962A and Y1019F mutants (Figure 4—figure supplement 1L and M).
evidence: This is a finding from co-IP experiments shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1L and M.

claim: SRC-1 phosphorylates the tyrosine residue of the CED-1 YXXL motif, which is required for CED-1 degradation.
source: These results confirmed that SRC-1 phosphorylated the tyrosine residue of the CED-1 YXXL motif, which is required for CED-1 degradation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the phosphorylation and degradation experiments.

claim: Inactivation of nck-1 increased the number of germline corpses in all three RNAi screen experiments.
source: To identify the adaptor protein containing an SH2 domain that could bind to the YXXL motif of CED-1, we generated RNAi knockdowns of 60 SH2 domain proteins and screened for germline cell death in three replicate experiments. This screen revealed that the inactivation of nck-1 increased the number of germline corpses in all three experiments (Table 5).
evidence: This is a finding from the SH2 domain protein RNAi screen shown in Table 5.

claim: NCK-1 interacts with CED-1-CT in yeast two-hybrid assays.
source: We also found that NCK-1 interacted with CED-1-CT in Y2H assays (Figure 5B)
evidence: This is a finding from Y2H assays shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Recombinant NCK-1 protein was efficiently pulled down by GST-CED-1-CT and GST-TRIM-21 but not by GST.
source: and that recombinant NCK-1 protein was efficiently pulled down by GST-CED-1-CT and GST-TRIM-21, but not by GST (Figure 5C)
evidence: This is a finding from GST pull-down assays shown in Figure 5C.

claim: NCK-1 directly interacts with the CED-1 intracellular domain and TRIM-21.
source: and that recombinant NCK-1 protein was efficiently pulled down by GST-CED-1-CT and GST-TRIM-21, but not by GST (Figure 5C), indicating that NCK-1 could directly interact with the CED-1 intracellular domain and TRIM-21.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the GST pull-down results.

claim: NCK-1 interaction with CED-1-CT and TRIM-21 was confirmed by TurboID proximity labeling.
source: These results confirmed co-IP with CED-1-CT or TRIM-21 tagged with TurboID ligase (Figure 5D and E).
evidence: This is a finding from TurboID proximity labeling shown in Figure 5D and E.

claim: Endogenous levels of CED-1 were increased in nck-1 knockdown worms.
source: In addition, we found that the endogenous levels of CED-1 were increased, whereas CED-1 poly-ubiquitination was reduced in nck-1 knockdown worms (Figure 5F and G).
evidence: This is a finding from Western blot analysis shown in Figure 5F.

claim: CED-1 poly-ubiquitination was reduced in nck-1 knockdown worms.
source: In addition, we found that the endogenous levels of CED-1 were increased, whereas CED-1 poly-ubiquitination was reduced in nck-1 knockdown worms (Figure 5F and G).
evidence: This is a finding from co-IP experiments shown in Figure 5G.

claim: nck-1 RNAi resulted in increased cell corpse counts in tissue-specific RNAi worms.
source: We observed that nck-1 RNAi also resulted in increased cell corpse counts in xwhIs49(rde-1; Pced-1::rde-1) transgenic worms with phagocyte-specific RNAi suppression (Figure 5H)
evidence: This is a finding from cell corpse counting shown in Figure 5H.

claim: nck-1 functions in cell corpse removal.
source: We observed that nck-1 RNAi also resulted in increased cell corpse counts in xwhIs49(rde-1; Pced-1::rde-1) transgenic worms with phagocyte-specific RNAi suppression (Figure 5H), suggesting that nck-1 functions in cell corpse removal.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the tissue-specific RNAi results.

claim: nck-1 RNAi increased cell corpse numbers in both ced-2(n1994) and ced-1(e1735) mutants.
source: Moreover, we found that nck-1 RNAi increased cell corpse numbers in both ced-2(n1994) and ced-1(e1735) mutants, suggesting that nck-1 does not act specifically within either pathway to regulate cell corpse removal (Figure 5I– and J).
evidence: This is a finding from cell corpse counting shown in Figure 5I and J.

claim: nck-1 does not act specifically within either engulfment pathway to regulate cell corpse removal.
source: Moreover, we found that nck-1 RNAi increased cell corpse numbers in both ced-2(n1994) and ced-1(e1735) mutants, suggesting that nck-1 does not act specifically within either pathway to regulate cell corpse removal (Figure 5I– and J).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the genetic interaction results.

claim: Endogenous levels of CED-1 were increased in nck-1(xwh51) mutants.
source: To further confirm these findings, we used CRISPR-Cas9 to generate a mutant allele of nck-1(xwh51) in which a premature stop codon was introduced at the N-terminus in WT worms (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A). We found that the endogenous levels of CED-1 were increased (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B)
evidence: This is a finding from Western blot analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Cell corpse numbers were increased in nck-1(xwh51) mutants.
source: We found that the endogenous levels of CED-1 were increased (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B), as were the cell corpse numbers, (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C) in nck-1(xwh51) mutants.
evidence: This is a finding from cell corpse counting shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The binding of TRIM-21 to CED-1 was substantially reduced in the nck-1(xwh51) background.
source: In addition, the binding of TRIM-21 to CED-1 was substantially reduced in the nck-1(xwh51) background (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D and E).
evidence: This is a finding from co-IP experiments shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1D and E.

claim: CED-1 poly-ubiquitination was reduced in nck-1(xwh51) worms.
source: Moreover, CED-1 poly-ubiquitination was reduced in nck-1(xwh51) worms (Figure 5—figure supplement 1E and F).
evidence: This is a finding from co-IP experiments shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1E and F.

claim: The interaction of NCK-1 to CED-1 was significantly reduced in Y1019F mutants compared to in the WT.
source: To investigate whether phosphorylation of CED-1 mediated its interaction with NCK-1, we created a Y1019F mutant of CED-1 (cannot be phosphorylated) under control of the CED-1 promoter. The interaction of NCK-1 to CED-1 was significantly reduced in Y1019F mutants compared to in the WT (Figure 5K)
evidence: This is a finding from co-IP experiments shown in Figure 5K.

claim: Phosphorylation of CED-1 is required to maintain its interaction with NCK-1.
source: The interaction of NCK-1 to CED-1 was significantly reduced in Y1019F mutants compared to in the WT (Figure 5K), indicating that phosphorylation of CED-1 is required to maintain its interaction with NCK-1.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the co-IP results with Y1019F mutant.

claim: The adaptor protein NCK-1 is required for CED-1 degradation through the proteasome pathway.
source: These results confirmed that the adaptor protein NCK-1 was required for CED-1 degradation through the proteasome pathway.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the nck-1 mutant and knockdown experiments.

claim: ubc-21(xwh16) and trim-21(xwh13) knockout lines contained significantly more cell corpses than WT at various embryonic stages and in adult germline cells.
source: To determine the roles of UBC-21 and TRIM-21 in cell corpse engulfment, we used CRISPR-Cas9 to generate ubc-21(xwh16) and trim-21(xwh13) knockout worms. We found that both knockout lines contained significantly more cell corpses than WT at various embryonic stages and in adult germline cells (Figure 6A, Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a finding from cell corpse counting shown in Figure 6A and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Cell corpses persisted significantly longer in trim-21(xwh13) mutants than in WT worms.
source: In addition, cell corpses persisted significantly longer in trim-21(xwh13) mutants than in WT worms (Figure 6B, Figure 6—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a finding from time-lapse microscopy shown in Figure 6B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The number of cell deaths in trim-21(xwh13) embryos was indistinguishable from that in the wild-type.
source: However, the number of cell deaths in trim-21(xwh13) embryos was indistinguishable from that in the wild-type (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is a finding from cell death counting shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Overexpression of TRIM-21 under the control of the CED-1 or heat shock promoter resulted in increased cell corpse numbers.
source: We also found that overexpression of TRIM-21 under the control of the CED-1 or heat shock promoter resulted in increased cell corpse numbers (Figure 6—figure supplement 1D–F).
evidence: This is a finding from cell corpse counting shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1D–F.

claim: The accumulation of cell corpses in trim-21 mutants resulted from defective corpse clearance rather than excessive apoptosis.
source: These findings indicated that the accumulation of cell corpses resulted from defective corpse clearance rather than excessive apoptosis.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the cell death and corpse persistence results.

claim: TRIM-21::mCherry was ubiquitously expressed in C. elegans and appeared to be localized in the cytoplasm.
source: To examine the subcellular localization and expression patterns of TRIM-21, we integrated a TRIM-21::mCherry fusion protein, under the control of its native promoter xwhIs33(Ptrim-21trim-21::mcherry), into the WT C. elegans genome. We observed that TRIM-21::mCherry was ubiquitously expressed in the worms and appeared to be localized in the cytoplasm.
evidence: This is a finding from fluorescence microscopy.

claim: In early larvae, TRIM-21::mCherry was mainly observed in pharyngeal muscle cells and body wall muscle cells.
source: In early larvae, TRIM-21::mCherry was mainly observed in pharyngeal muscle cells and body wall muscle cells (Figure 6—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: This is a finding from fluorescence microscopy shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1G.

claim: Overexpression of CED-1 enhanced the cell corpse phenotype in the trim-21 mutant.
source: However, we found that overexpression of CED-1 enhanced the cell corpse phenotype in the trim-21 mutant (Figure 6—figure supplement 1H).
evidence: This is a finding from cell corpse counting shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1H.

claim: Extra-chromosomal expression of TRIM-21::GFP driven by its native promoter completely rescued cell corpse clearance in trim-21(xwh13) worms.
source: To test whether TRIM-21 could reverse the engulfment defects in a trim-21(xwh13) mutant, we observed the extra-chromosomal expression of TRIM-21::GFP driven by its native promoter (Ptrim-21trim-21::gfp) and found complete rescue of cell corpse clearance in trim-21(xwh13) worms (Figure 6—figure supplement 1I and J).
evidence: This is a finding from cell corpse counting shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1I and J.

claim: Expression of hTRIM21 driven by the trim-21 promoter effectively rescued the defective corpse clearance phenotype of trim-21(xwh13).
source: We found a high level of conservation between TRIM-21 from C. elegans and its homolog, hTRIM21, in humans. Expression of hTRIM21 driven by the trim-21 promoter effectively rescued the defective corpse clearance phenotype of trim-21(xwh13) (Figure 6—figure supplement 1K)
evidence: This is a finding from cell corpse counting shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1K.

claim: Human TRIM21 can functionally substitute for worm TRIM-21 in the cell corpse removal process.
source: Expression of hTRIM21 driven by the trim-21 promoter effectively rescued the defective corpse clearance phenotype of trim-21(xwh13) (Figure 6—figure supplement 1K), showing that human TRIM21 could functionally substitute for worm TRIM-21 in the cell corpse removal process.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the rescue experiment with human TRIM21.

claim: ubc-21; trim-21 double mutants did not exhibit altered defects in cell corpse clearance compared to single mutants.
source: To demonstrate that trim-21, ubc-21, and ced-1 function in the same genetic pathway, we found that ubc-21; trim-21 double mutants in either the ubc-21(xwh16) or trim-21(xwh13) strains did not exhibit altered defects in cell corpse clearance (Figure 6A, Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a finding from cell corpse counting shown in Figure 6A and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A.

claim: TRIM-21 and UBC-21 act together to promote AC clearance.
source: These data indicated that TRIM-21 and UBC-21 acted together to promote AC clearance.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the double mutant results.

claim: Loss of trim-21 or ubc-21 function did not further increase the accumulation of corpses in ced-1(e1735) germline cells.
source: In addition, the loss of trim-21 or ubc-21 function did not further increase the accumulation of corpses in ced-1(e1735) germline cells (Figure 6C, Figure 6—figure supplement 1L)
evidence: This is a finding from cell corpse counting shown in Figure 6C and Figure 6—figure supplement 1L.

claim: trim-21, ubc-21, and ced-1 probably function in the same genetic pathway.
source: In addition, the loss of trim-21 or ubc-21 function did not further increase the accumulation of corpses in ced-1(e1735) germline cells (Figure 6C, Figure 6—figure supplement 1L), suggesting that trim-21, ubc-21, and ced-1 probably function in the same genetic pathway.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the genetic interaction results.

claim: Cell corpses in ubc-21(xwh16) and trim-21(xwh13) germline cells and embryos were surrounded by CED-1::GFP phagocytic receptor–reporter fusion protein, just as in WT.
source: Fluorescence microscopic observation of the ubc-21(xwh16) and trim-21(xwh13) germline cells and embryos indicated that cell corpses were surrounded by CED-1::GFP phagocytic receptor–reporter fusion protein, just as in WT (Figure 6D, F, and G, Figure 6—figure supplement 1M and N)
evidence: This is a finding from fluorescence microscopy shown in Figure 6D, F, and G, and Figure 6—figure supplement 1M and N.

claim: Recognition and initiation of engulfment were unaffected by the knockout of ubc-21 or trim-21.
source: Fluorescence microscopic observation of the ubc-21(xwh16) and trim-21(xwh13) germline cells and embryos indicated that cell corpses were surrounded by CED-1::GFP phagocytic receptor–reporter fusion protein, just as in WT (Figure 6D, F, and G, Figure 6—figure supplement 1M and N), which suggested that recognition and initiation of engulfment were unaffected by the knockout of either gene.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the CED-1::GFP localization results.

claim: Phagosome association with LAAT-1 was significantly reduced in both ubc-21(xwh16) and trim-21(xwh13) mutants.
source: Next, we individually integrated a panel of GFP- or mCHERRY-tagged phagosomal markers into the ubc-21(xwh16) and trim-21(xwh13) mutants, respectively, and found that phagosome association with LAAT-1, a lysosomal membrane protein (Liu et al., 2012), was significantly reduced in both the ubc-21(xwh16) and trim-21(xwh13) mutants (Figure 6E–G, Figure 6—figure supplement 1M and N).
evidence: This is a finding from fluorescence microscopy shown in Figure 6E–G and Figure 6—figure supplement 1M and N.

claim: The signal from NUC-1 and CPL-1 was significantly decreased on phagosomes in the ubc-21(xwh16) and trim-21(xwh13) mutants.
source: Moreover, the signal from NUC-1, a lysosomal DNase, and CPL-1, a lysosomal cathepsin protease, was also significantly decreased on phagosomes in the ubc-21(xwh16) and trim-21(xwh13) mutants (Figure 6E–G, Figure 6—figure supplement 1M and N).
evidence: This is a finding from fluorescence microscopy shown in Figure 6E–G and Figure 6—figure supplement 1M and N.

claim: Loss of ubc-21(xwh16) and trim-21(xwh13) impaired phagosome maturation at a later stage.
source: These data showed that the loss of ubc-21(xwh16) and trim-21(xwh13) impaired phagosome maturation at a later stage.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the phagosomal marker results.

claim: AO staining was greatly reduced in trim-21(xwh13) mutants compared with WT worms.
source: To test whether the persistence of cell corpses in trim-21(xwh13) mutants resulted from a failure in the acidification of phagosomes containing cell corpses (i.e., a late stage of corpse clearance), acridine orange (AO) staining was used to highlight compromised cell corpses. We found that AO staining was greatly reduced in trim-21(xwh13) mutants compared with the WT worms (Figure 6H)
evidence: This is a finding from AO staining shown in Figure 6H.

claim: Loss of trim-21(xwh13) affected the acidification of cell corpse-containing phagosomes.
source: We found that AO staining was greatly reduced in trim-21(xwh13) mutants compared with the WT worms (Figure 6H), suggesting that the loss of trim-21(xwh13) affected the acidification of cell corpse-containing phagosomes.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the AO staining results.

claim: In wild-type, chromatin in early germ cell corpses was condensed and disappeared within 60 min (54.6 ± 4.44 min; n = 5).
source: To directly monitor the degradation process of cell corpses, we introduced a germline-specific transgenic marker for chromatin, H2B::mCHERRY, into trim-21(xwh16) mutants. We found that in the wild-type the chromatin in early germ cell corpses was condensed and disappeared within 60 min (54.6 ± 4.44 min; n = 5).
evidence: This is a finding from time-lapse microscopy.

claim: In trim-21(xwh13) mutants, chromatin in early germ cell corpses was condensed but diffused throughout the corpse in later stages, and the mCHERRY signal persisted for 90 min (90.2 ± 8.10 min, n = 5).
source: In contrast, although the chromatin in early germ cell corpses of trim-21(xwh13) mutants was also condensed, it diffused throughout the corpse in the later stages of phagosome maturation, and the mCHERRY signal persisted for 90 min (90.2 ± 8.10 min, n = 5) (Figure 6I, Figure 6—figure supplement 1O)
evidence: This is a finding from time-lapse microscopy shown in Figure 6I and Figure 6—figure supplement 1O.

claim: Chromatin degradation was greatly delayed in cell corpses of trim-21(xwh13) mutants.
source: In contrast, although the chromatin in early germ cell corpses of trim-21(xwh13) mutants was also condensed, it diffused throughout the corpse in the later stages of phagosome maturation, and the mCHERRY signal persisted for 90 min (90.2 ± 8.10 min, n = 5) (Figure 6I, Figure 6—figure supplement 1O), indicating that chromatin degradation was greatly delayed in the cell corpses of the mutant strain.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the time-lapse microscopy results.

claim: The accumulation of cell corpses caused by the trim-21 mutation was due to defects in cell corpse digestion in engulfing cells.
source: Collectively, these findings demonstrated that the accumulation of cell corpses caused by the trim-21 mutation was due to defects in cell corpse digestion in engulfing cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the phagosome maturation and acidification results.

claim: VHA-10 subunit G was identified as an interaction partner of CED-1-CT by LC-MS/MS.
source: In total, 15 proteins were identified as interaction partners of CED-1-CT (Table 6), with endosome system proteins representing the most attractive candidates. Interestingly, VHA-10 subunit G was identified as an interaction partner of CED-1-CT (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is a finding from LC-MS/MS analysis shown in Table 6 and Figure 7B.

claim: The direct interaction between CED-1-CT and VHA-10 was confirmed by GST pull-down assay and proximity biotin labeling.
source: We further confirmed the direct interaction between CED-1-CT and VHA-10 by GST pull-down assay and proximity biotin labeling (Figure 7C and D).
evidence: This is a finding from GST pull-down and proximity labeling shown in Figure 7C and D.

claim: vha-10 knockdown by RNAi resulted in increased germ cell corpse number.
source: VHA-10 is an ortholog of human ATPase H+ transporting V1 subunit G2. This VHA subunit performs the same function across a multitude of essential cellular processes, such as acidification of lysosomes and intracellular organelles (Collins and Forgac, 2020). V-ATPase-mediated acidification of lysosomes is required for the activation of lysosomal hydrolases and ultimately leads to the enzymatic degradation of the cell corpse (Ernstrom et al., 2012). We found that vha-10 knockdown by RNAi resulted in the increased germ cell corpse number (Figure 7E)
evidence: This is a finding from cell corpse counting shown in Figure 7E.

claim: vha-10 knockdown resulted in delayed clearance of dying or dead cells.
source: We found that vha-10 knockdown by RNAi resulted in the increased germ cell corpse number (Figure 7E) due to delayed clearance of dying or dead cells (Figure 7F).
evidence: This is a finding from time-lapse microscopy shown in Figure 7F.

claim: vha-10 knockdown did not affect corpse clearance defects in the trim-21(xwh13) mutant strain.
source: We next examined the effects of VHA-10 on TRIM-21-mediated corpse clearance and found that vha-10 knockdown did not affect corpse clearance defects in the trim-21(xwh13) mutant strain, suggesting that trim-21 and vha-10 likely function in the same genetic pathway (Figure 7E).
evidence: This is a finding from cell corpse counting shown in Figure 7E.

claim: trim-21 and vha-10 likely function in the same genetic pathway.
source: We next examined the effects of VHA-10 on TRIM-21-mediated corpse clearance and found that vha-10 knockdown did not affect corpse clearance defects in the trim-21(xwh13) mutant strain, suggesting that trim-21 and vha-10 likely function in the same genetic pathway (Figure 7E).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the genetic interaction results.

claim: Knockdown of vha-10 impaired phagosome maturation at a late stage.
source: In addition, the knockdown of vha-10 impaired phagosome maturation at a late stage as well as the acidification of phagosomes containing cell corpses (Figure 7G and H), which was similar to the phenotype of trim-21 loss-of-function mutants.
evidence: This is a finding from phagosomal marker analysis shown in Figure 7G and H.

claim: Knockdown of vha-10 impaired acidification of phagosomes containing cell corpses.
source: In addition, the knockdown of vha-10 impaired phagosome maturation at a late stage as well as the acidification of phagosomes containing cell corpses (Figure 7G and H), which was similar to the phenotype of trim-21 loss-of-function mutants.
evidence: This is a finding from AO staining shown in Figure 7H.

claim: VHA-10 overexpression fully attenuated the increased cell corpse phenotype in trim-21(xwh13) mutants.
source: To address whether the dysfunction of vha-10 was responsible for the defects in cell corpse degradation in trim-21 mutants, we overexpressed VHA-10 by placing it under the control of the ced-1 promoter (Pced-1vha-10::mcherry) in trim-21(xwh13) mutant animals. Interestingly, VHA-10 overexpression fully attenuated the increased cell corpse phenotype and completely restored the acidification of phagosome defects in trim-21(xwh13) mutants (Figure 7I and J)
evidence: This is a finding from cell corpse counting shown in Figure 7I.

claim: VHA-10 overexpression completely restored the acidification of phagosome defects in trim-21(xwh13) mutants.
source: Interestingly, VHA-10 overexpression fully attenuated the increased cell corpse phenotype and completely restored the acidification of phagosome defects in trim-21(xwh13) mutants (Figure 7I and J)
evidence: This is a finding from AO staining shown in Figure 7J.

claim: VHA-10 dysfunction in engulfing cells causes defects in cell corpse degradation exhibited by trim-21 mutants.
source: Interestingly, VHA-10 overexpression fully attenuated the increased cell corpse phenotype and completely restored the acidification of phagosome defects in trim-21(xwh13) mutants (Figure 7I and J), indicating that VHA-10 dysfunction in engulfing cells caused defects in cell corpse degradation exhibited by trim-21 mutants.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the VHA-10 overexpression rescue results.

claim: Recruitment and release of CED-1::GFP to cell corpses in trim-21 (8.29 ± 0.48 min, n = 5) was similar to that in WT (8.31 ± 0.25 min, n = 5) but not to that in snx-1 (>30 min, n = 5).
source: We next investigated CED-1 recycling in the trim-21 mutant. Recruitment and release of CED-1::GFP to cell corpses in trim-21 (8.29 ± 0.48 min, n = 5) was similar to that in the WT (8.31 ± 0.25 min, n = 5) but not to that in snx-1 (>30 min, n = 5) (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a finding from time-lapse microscopy shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1A.

claim: CED-1::GFP levels in trim-21 mutants were comparable to those in N2 on plasma membranes, phagosomal membranes, and phagolysosomal membranes.
source: To confirm whether CED-1 was indeed degraded by proteasomes in addition to lysosomal degradation during phagosome maturation, we examined CED-1::GFP levels on the plasma membranes, phagosomal membranes, and phagolysosomal membranes in trim-21 and snx-1 mutants and in double mutants lacking both TRIM-21 and SNX-1. The CED-1::GFP levels in the trim-21 mutants were comparable to those on the N2 in plasma membranes, phagosomal membranes, and phagolysosomal membranes, whereas snx-1 mutants and trim-21; snx-1 double mutants exhibited lower CED-1::GFP levels (Figure 7—figure supplement 1B–E).
evidence: This is a finding from fluorescence microscopy shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1B–E.

claim: snx-1 mutants and trim-21; snx-1 double mutants exhibited lower CED-1::GFP levels on membranes.
source: The CED-1::GFP levels in the trim-21 mutants were comparable to those on the N2 in plasma membranes, phagosomal membranes, and phagolysosomal membranes, whereas snx-1 mutants and trim-21; snx-1 double mutants exhibited lower CED-1::GFP levels (Figure 7—figure supplement 1B–E).
evidence: This is a finding from fluorescence microscopy shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1B–E.

claim: Co-localization of CED-1 and VHA-10 on phagosomes was dramatically increased in trim-21 and snx-1 mutants compared to in the WT.
source: In addition, co-localization of CED-1 and VHA-10 on phagosomes was dramatically increased in trim-21 and snx-1 mutants compared to in the WT (Figure 7—figure supplement 2A–C).
evidence: This is a finding from fluorescence microscopy shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 2A–C.

claim: A similar CED-1-VHA-10 interaction was observed in snx-1 mutants and the WT.
source: To further verify whether the interaction between CED-1 and VHA-10 varied in the trim-21 or snx-1 mutants, we inserted an HA tag into the endogenous vha-10 loci using CRISPR-Cas9 to generate C. elegans strains xwh52(ha::vha-10) (Figure 7—figure supplement 2D). A similar CED-1-VHA-10 interaction was observed in snx-1 mutants and the WT; this interaction was greatly enhanced in trim-21 mutants (Figure 7—figure supplement 2E and F)
evidence: This is a finding from co-IP experiments shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 2E and F.

claim: CED-1-VHA-10 interaction was greatly enhanced in trim-21 mutants.
source: A similar CED-1-VHA-10 interaction was observed in snx-1 mutants and the WT; this interaction was greatly enhanced in trim-21 mutants (Figure 7—figure supplement 2E and F)
evidence: This is a finding from co-IP experiments shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 2E and F.

claim: Excessive CED-1 in trim-21 mutants bound VHA-10, unlike in snx-1 mutants.
source: A similar CED-1-VHA-10 interaction was observed in snx-1 mutants and the WT; this interaction was greatly enhanced in trim-21 mutants (Figure 7—figure supplement 2E and F), suggesting that excessive CED-1 in the trim-21 mutants bound VHA-10, unlike in the snx-1 mutants.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the co-IP results comparing trim-21 and snx-1 mutants.

claim: Excess CED-1, which accumulated in trim-21 mutants, bound to the VHA-10 subunit of V-ATPase, negatively affected the acidification of phagosomes, and consequently blocked cell corpse degradation.
source: Taken together, excess CED-1, which accumulated in trim-21 mutants, bound to the VHA-10 subunit of V-ATPase, negatively affected the acidification of phagosomes, and consequently blocked cell corpse degradation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the VHA-10 interaction and rescue experiments.

claim: TRIM-21-mediated proteasome degradation of CED-1 occurs independently of lysosomal degradation of CED-1 through loss of function of the retromer complex.
source: Additionally, TRIM-21-mediated proteasome degradation of CED-1 occurs independently of lysosomal degradation of CED-1 through loss of function of the retromer complex.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the vps-37 knockdown experiments.
